raw: {"mode":"iff","restated":"∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∀ S : Set (Fin n → ℝ), Convex ℝ S → IsCompact S → (interior S).Nonempty → barycenter S = 0 → {z : Fin n → ℤ | (fun i => (z i : ℝ)) ∈ interior S} = {0} → ((MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) S).toReal ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ)","proof":"exact Iff.rfl","english":"For n ≥ 1, every convex compact set S in ℝⁿ with nonempty interior and barycenter 0, whose only interior integer lattice point is the origin, has Lebesgue volume at most (n+1)^n / n!.","why_clearer":"It unfolds normalizedVolume into the real part of Lebesgue measure and interiorLatticePoints/integerPoint into an explicit set of integer vectors whose real coordinates lie in the interior of S, so no bespoke definitions remain except barycenter."}

parsed.restated: ∀ {n : ℕ}, 0 < n → ∀ S : Set (Fin n → ℝ), Convex ℝ S → IsCompact S → (interior S).Nonempty → barycenter S = 0 → {z : Fin n → ℤ | (fun i => (z i : ℝ)) ∈ interior S} = {0} → ((MeasureTheory.volume : MeasureTheory.Measure (Fin n → ℝ)) S).toReal ≤ ((n : ℝ) + 1) ^ n / (n.factorial : ℝ)
parsed.english: For n ≥ 1, every convex compact set S in ℝⁿ with nonempty interior and barycenter 0, whose only interior integer lattice point is the origin, has Lebesgue volume at most (n+1)^n / n!.
parsed.why_clearer: It unfolds normalizedVolume into the real part of Lebesgue measure and interiorLatticePoints/integerPoint into an explicit set of integer vectors whose real coordinates lie in the interior of S, so no bespoke definitions remain except barycenter.
